thread:
Eli: Heads-upwe're seeing inconsistent behavior when a model is pinned in hosted but a dedicated fallback picks a different quantized variant. Pin is set, but enforcement differs. Anyone seen this?
Priya: yep. root cause is two meanings of "pin": intent (user says keep this model available) vs enforcement (runtime must keep weights resident). We need to separate them.
Noah: big +1. Propose "intent-first" model: control plane records intent with version metadata; runtimes get short-lived signed lease to enforce.
Marta: curious about the signed lease format. can we standardize a compact proto that includes: model_id, model_hash, memory_estimate, expires_at, issuer, signature?
Eli: exactly. minimal example (pseudo-json):
```
{"model":"rw-7b-v1","hash":"abc123","mem_mb":"42000","exp":"2024-11-01T12:00:00Z","iss":"controlplane","sig":"..."}
```
Priya: for private installs, control plane might be unreachable. solution: export the intent bundle and let customer KMS sign a local lease. runtime accepts either control-signed or customer-signed leases based on install mode.
Noah: edge cases: what if intent is revoked upstream but private node still has an active lease? we need revocation semantics. options: short TTL + explicit revocation list (RDL) that can be pulled on periodic sync.
Marta: short TTL + heartbeat seems simpler. runtime treats lease as authoritative only until expiry unless it receives an RDL entry. RDL signed by controlplane too.
Eli: revocation race: imagine ops revokes but node offline. customer operator should be able to apply a local override (signed by customer KMS) to unpin immediately. we must log the provenance chain.
Priya: agree. logs should include lease_id, issuer (control/customer), action, and reason. include variant selection rationale when fallback occurs.
Noah: operationally, we must avoid evicting during transient network flaps. so lease TTL > failover detection window. propose default TTL 15m, with renew every 5m.
Marta: for high-cost models we might want explicit long-term pin (monthly) that requires manual billing commit. treat that as a different intent type: "financial-pin" that sets quota and billing lock.
Eli: good call. intent types: pin, financial-pin, warm-cache (soft). runtime enforcement differs per type.
Priya: API proposal: POST /pins returns lease OR intent-ack. GET /pins?tenant=.. returns current intent + signatures for active leases. include audit_id.
Noah: include a small schema for lease signatures: ed25519 over canonicalized lease JSON; header contains issuer_kid and expiry. runtime library must verify ed25519 and reject old canonicalization forms.
Marta: POC notes: I'll mock a private install: export intent bundle, sign with local KMS (aws-kms/softHSM), import to node, and validate enforcement. I'll wire basic logs: "selected-variant=quant8-lite reason=memory-sparse lease=lease-789 issuer=customer-kms"
Eli: action items: Marta POC, Noah write lease-spec (sig format + canonicalization), Priya draft API surface and billing pin semantics. I'll open a follow-up ticket linking tasks.
Priya: also flag telemetry needs: per-lease renews, revocations, enforcement decisions, and fallback reasons (latency/capacity/mem).
Noah: who will draft the RFC? I can take a first pass and include the state machine (intent -> lease-issue -> renew -> revoke), and couple of sequence diagrams (online vs offline).
Marta: I'll add a tiny go library skeleton for runtime verification: VerifyLease(leaseBlob, rootKeys) -> (ok, issuer, expiry, reason).
ops-bot: deploy: leases-api v2024.11.0 promoted to prod in hosted. No downtime.
Eli: thanks bot. let's not forget user-facing docs for the pin UI (billing implications).
Priya: noted. I'll coordinate with docs/ux. :white_check_mark:
Eli: cool, wrapping up. we'll keep the lease format minimal and iterative.
Noah: putting RFC draft in docs/rfcs/lease-intent.md, pinging on PR.
Marta: starting POC later today, will post results in #eng-runtime.
